newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Top Colombian drug lords said worth $200 billion.
newsitem.headline: Top Colombian drug lords said worth $200 billion.

text.p: Colombia's top drug lords are worth a combined total of $200 billion, the country's prestigious weekly news magazine Semana said on Tuesday.

The figure was based on a study by the Justice Ministry that calculated how much money might enter government coffers if Colombia's Congress passed an asset forfeiture law allowing for the seizure of ill-gotten property. Justice Ministry spokesmen could not be reached for immediate comment.
Semana said brothers Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela and two other reputed traffickers, Pastor Perafan and Jesus Amado Sarria, had a combined worth of at least $50 billion.

Perafan, a former army sergeant with businesses in Colombia, Madrid, Rome and Moscow, is the target if a nationwide manhunt. Sarria, a former police sergeant, was jailed last year as were the Rodriguez Orejuelas -- undisputed leaders of the powerful Cali cocaine cartel.
